design:
Judged from cred-clarity.json and cred-safety.json (see judgement): the engine is the safety design's, the words and screens the clarity design's, plus four gaps neither closed.

1. WHAT A PERSON CAN HAVE. At most one Claude subscription (through Claude Code, no money per use within the plan's limits) and one API key (money per use). Plan credits, never saved today, follow the API key wherever it goes.

2. THE ONE CHOICE. Settings -> Basics -> 'Which Claude does the work', right under Accounts and keys. It replaces Advanced's order list ('Claude: which to use first') and the row 'When my first choice runs out mid-session'. One intro line: 'Your Claude subscription has no cost per use within your plan's limits; your API key costs money per use.' Five presets, each a label that shows the order and one line:
 (a) 'Subscription first, then wait': 'When your subscription runs out, work waits until it is back. Nothing moves to your API key.'
 (b) 'Subscription first, ask before API key': 'When your subscription runs out, one card asks: go on with your API key at its cost, or wait.'
 (c) 'Subscription first, then API key': 'When your subscription runs out, your API key takes over at once. You are told the cost.'
 (d) 'API key first, then subscription': 'Your API key does the work, at a cost per use. When it runs out, your subscription takes over.'
 (e) 'API key only': 'Your API key does all the work, at a cost per use. When it runs out, work waits.'
Below them: the credentials in the order the choice gives, one row each with its role ('Does the work' / 'After you say yes, when your subscription runs out' / 'Takes over when your subscription runs out' / 'Only for a task your subscription cannot do' / 'Not used'), its state now ('Works now' / 'At its limit until 15:40' / 'Share used until Tue 1 Dec' / 'Refused: save a new sign-in' [link] / 'Not saved') and its month ('34% of this month's allowance used' / 'CHF 2.10 this month'); one line, computed when shown, of what happens next ('If your subscription runs out, you are asked before your API key is used.'; while it is out: 'Your subscription is at its limit until 15:40. Answer the card to use your API key, or wait. [Answer]'; with a yes standing: 'Your API key does the work until 15:40: you said yes. [Stop using it]'); one line 'Runs out means: its usage limit is reached, the share of your subscription Forerunner may use is used, or Anthropic refuses it.'; for the subscription-first presets one footnote 'A task only your API key can do here (one that must ask you) still runs on it; the plan card says so.' With one credential saved the presets fold away into one sentence ('Only your Claude subscription is saved: it does the work, and when it runs out work waits until it resets. Save an API key to choose what happens then. [Save an API key]'); the stored choice is kept for when the second is saved. A person who never set an order sees no preset checked and one line above them: 'Not chosen yet: tasks use your subscription first; chat, planning and reviews use your API key first. When one runs out, the work waits.' ('... goes on with the other one.' under today's use_other). A choice that moves less onto money acts at once; one that moves more onto money without asking (to (c), (d) or (e) from a preset that moves less) asks once: 'Use "Subscription first, then API key"? When your subscription runs out, work goes on with your API key at once, at a cost per use. [Change] [Cancel]'. Changes lists each change with Undo (an Undo that moves more onto money asks the same yes). Chat can change it in words with the same read-back; no agent, specialist, task check, card, page or file can set it. Stored as human.notify_prefs.credential_policy, one of subscription_then_wait, subscription_then_ask, subscription_then_key, key_then_subscription, key_only.

3. MIGRATION, nothing a person chose changes. Until a preset is stored, the policy is read at every pick from today's two settings and nothing is rewritten: billing_order with the subscription first + wait -> (a); + use_other -> (c); the API key or plan credits first + wait -> (e); + use_other -> (d); no billing_order -> not chosen: today's split order (tasks subscription first; chat, planning, reviews, the task check and the jobs CALL_FALLBACK_ORDER) with the rule from mid_session_limit (wait, or next for use_other). The one change for everyone is 7b's: under wait, chat, planning and reviews whose first choice stopped now wait too instead of moving. Once a preset is stored it wins; settings.set billing_order or mid_session_limit, and an Undo of an old row of either, are refused with 'This was replaced by "Which Claude does the work"; change it there.'; both keys leave the chat model's settings tool; POST /settings/billing-order still works and stores the preset with the order changed and the rule kept. Budget cards at the share filed before the upgrade keep going on at the month's start.

4. WHAT A STOP IS, and when it ends. Four stops, each with a stop key computed from the row: a usage limit as the provider reports it (Claude Code's limit, the API's spend limit, spend cap or credit balance; ends at the reported reset, else after an hour, ADR 0100 point 4; key 'limit:<until>'); Forerunner's share of the subscription (ends at the month's start or when the person raises the allowance; key 'share:<month>:<allowance>'); a key's own monthly cap (dormant: no screen sets one; ends at the month's start; key 'key_month:<month>:<cap>'); a refusal (a 401 or 403 key, an expired sign-in; ends when a different credential is saved; key 'refused:<refusedAt>'). Not stops and never a reason to switch: the person's monthly cap, a project's, session's or task's budget (no switch helps: subscription spend counts against them as its API-equivalent; ADR 0112's pause as today), a throttle (retried once at once), a credential not saved or turned off.

5. WHAT THE ENGINE DOES, for every model call: task runs, the critic's reviews, the plan from a brief and Change the plan, D7's task check, chat and the background jobs. The policy gives the order and the rule; the chooser's rule stays (a task only one credential can do properly runs there), and at a stop a task never moves to a credential that does less of what it needs: it waits and its row says why ('Waits for your API key: only it can read web pages here.'), so the plan card's 'only it can' stays true. When the credential a call would use first has stopped:
 - next ((c), (d), and not chosen with use_other): the next credential serves at once. If it has stopped too, the work waits for whichever comes back first.
 - ask ((b)): nothing moves until the person says yes for this stop. Then the other credential serves every kind of call until the stop ends (a grant). Before the yes the work waits exactly as under wait, and one card asks (point 7).
 - wait ((a), (e), and not chosen by default): nothing calls the other credential, for any purpose. Work whose first choice is the other credential (the chooser) runs.
In code: the router holds every stop (resting, refused, plan_share, monthly_limit) with its until and stop key under ask and wait (whenStopped replaces waitOnRest); a grant whose stop key is the current one lets the granted kind serve; RouterTaskBilling passes the sources excluded on this call to the router as held stops (today they are withheld before it) and never falls to a lower chooser group at a stop; RoutedProvider, after it rests or marks a source, picks again under the rule and under ask and wait ends the call with the wait, which each caller already handles (the review waits in review without a counted try, the plan waits, chat holds, a job skips). CALL_FALLBACK_ORDER stays only for the never-chosen split.

6. A TASK STOPPED MID-RUN. The run stops where it is (the hooks stop it at the limit or the share; nothing is passed), its work is kept (the work-in-progress commit on its branch, or the folder), no try is counted, nothing is reviewed. Under next, or after a yes, it goes back to the head of the session's queue and continues on the next credential in the same session (owner 7a: the task completed by the API), briefed in exact words: '## Where the last run stopped' / 'The last run of this task stopped when its Claude credential reached its limit, before its work was done. Its work so far is in the folder you work in (kept as a commit of its own): continue from it, do not start again.' ('was refused' / 'reached the share of the subscription Forerunner may use'), then its report or handoff as data and the files it changed; never '## The previous attempt / It failed'. Under wait, or before a yes, it waits; the session goes on with what can run and, when nothing can, ends 'Stopped to wait for a Claude credential' with the wait entry naming it; at the stop's end the session the person started goes on (d1109-starts-engine's continuation); no new session starts unless the person says so or turned on the hands-off setting. Forerunner's share reached mid-run is the same stop with reason share: no budget card, the session does not end for it, the rule decides; raising the allowance ends it.

7. ASK FIRST, the card word for word. One card per stop, for every project, filed only when work needs it (a task run, a review, planning, the task check; never for a chat question alone or a background job), and only when the API key can serve now and the caps have room for the waiting work's next call. It shows in Needs you, the Home list, the project status 'Waiting for you: use your API key?' [Answer], and the run indicator of a session that waits on it.
 Title 'Use your API key until 15:40?' ('... until Wed 12 Nov, 05:00?', '... until Tue 1 Dec?').
 Body 'Your Claude subscription is at its limit until 15:40. Going on with your API key costs about CHF 0.90 for "Style the page" and 2 more.' (the share: 'Forerunner has used the share of your subscription you allow this month. Going on ...'; a plan: '... costs about CHF 0.05 to draft the plan for "Quote page".'). The figure is the Start check's estimate of the waiting work, never above what is left of its session's work budget.
 Use API key: 'Work goes on now with your API key until 15:40, about CHF 0.90.'
 Wait: 'Nothing moves. At 15:40 your session goes on with your subscription.' (no session waits: 'Nothing moves. After 15:40 the work runs at your next Start.'; the share: 'Nothing moves until Tue 1 Dec, or until you raise the allowance in Settings.').
 Use API key writes the grant on the subscription's row (this stop only), then: the waiting tasks of a session that still runs go back into it as its own tasks; a session that ended to wait goes on now as the person's own start; a plan that waited is drafted; work waiting outside a person's session stays ready for the next Start. Done 'Done: your API key does the work until 15:40; your session goes on now.' (no session: 'Done: your API key does the work until 15:40; it runs at your next Start.'). Wait records the answer, so no second card comes for this stop; nothing moves; Done 'Done: nothing moves. Your session goes on at 15:40 with your subscription.' Unanswered, the card stays and nothing moves. A second or late answer changes nothing and shows the card's Done line. When the stop ends (the reset, the month, a raised allowance, a new credential) the grant ends with it and an open card closes: 'Closed: your Claude subscription can work again.'; when the API key stops too: 'Closed: your API key cannot be used now either; the work waits for whichever comes back first.'; a change of preset closes it and ends a grant. The Start dialog asks in place (point 10).

8. A REFUSAL (7c) follows the same rule as running out and always informs: one card per refusal (two refusals at once file one), one urgent notification (the card's), the link 'Save a new sign-in' / 'Save a new key' to the setup assistant. Its body says why in plain words from a category of Anthropic's answer, never its text ('The sign-in has expired or was signed out.', 'The key is not valid or was deleted.', 'The key may not use this model or workspace.', else 'Anthropic did not accept it.'), then what the work does under the rule: wait '... Save a new one in Settings; until then the work waits.'; next '... Save a new one in Settings; until then your API key does the work, at a cost per use.' (a refused key: '... until then your Claude subscription does the work.'); ask '... Save a new one in Settings, or go on with your API key until then (about CHF 0.90).' with Use API key / Wait; after an answer the card stays as the fix-it card, without options, until a new credential is saved. The second choice refused while the first works: '... Save a new one in Settings to use it again; your subscription goes on with the work.' A refused credential is never called again until a different one is saved, by no path (a switch, a grant, a continuation, a late answer, chat, a job, the probe): one 401 per credential, nothing that could lock the account.

9. A SWITCH IS TRANSPARENT (next, or a yes): data first (the run row names the source it ran on and switchedFrom {kind, stop}; billing.switch and billing.back session events; SessionResult.switched with the CHF the ledger booked; Costs by credential), then words: the session log once per stop '"Style the page" goes on with your API key from where it stopped: your subscription is at its limit until 15:40.' (later tasks as detail lines); the session page under its spend 'On your API key since 14:20 (your subscription's limit): CHF 0.42 so far.'; the result 'Your API key took over at 14:20 (your subscription's limit): CHF 0.42 of CHF 0.62.'; the task drawer's run 'On your API key after your subscription's limit · CHF 0.43'; the run indicator 'Quote page · the coder works on "Style the page" on your API key · 4 min'; Costs 'By credential'. A move onto money the policy made by itself inside a running session sends one notification per stop and session: 'Quote page: work goes on with your API key' / 'Your Claude subscription is at its limit until 15:40. Your API key costs money: about CHF 0.90 for what is left.'. None for the person's own yes, for a Start whose dialog said it, for a move onto the subscription (no money), or for a wait. When the first choice serves again a running session says once 'Your Claude subscription can work again; the next tasks use it.' and the next task uses it; a run is never moved mid-way (ADR 0100 point 3).

10. WHERE THE PERSON SEES IT. The Start dialog, one line under the plan sentence: 'If your subscription runs out, you are asked before your API key is used.' / '..., the work goes on with your API key (costs money).' / '..., the work waits for it.' / 'If your API key runs out, the work goes on with your subscription.' / 'If your API key runs out, the work waits for it.' (nothing with one credential). With the first choice stopped: under next 'Your subscription is at its limit until 15:40, so this runs on your API key (about CHF 0.90).'; under ask and wait two buttons, 'Use API key' ('Runs now on your API key until 15:40, about CHF 0.90; nothing passes this session's budget.') and 'Start at 15:40' ('Runs on your subscription once it is back.'), the one the preset leans to first (ask: Use API key; wait: Start at 15:40); 'Use API key' writes the same grant as the card and closes it; neither when the API key cannot serve or the caps have no room. The plan card: the same line once at its foot. Task rows and the project status: every wait in words ('Waits until Tue 1 Dec (your subscription's share)' [Change the allowance], 'Waits for your answer: use your API key?' [Answer], 'Waits for your API key: only it can read web pages here.'). The Inbox: the ask card and the refused card. Chat: under wait, or under ask before a yes, no model call; the reply 'Your Claude subscription is at its limit until 15:40, so I have not answered. I can still add, move and start tasks.' with one press 'Use API key' ('Answers this question on your API key: about CHF 0.02.'), which answers that one question only; under next or a standing yes, chat answers on the other one and its note says once 'Answered with your API key: your subscription is at its limit until 15:40.'. Background jobs never ask and never switch under ask or wait: they spend nothing, log one line and run at their next time after the stop. No reminder and no app-wide bar for a wait (the owner: 'We don't need notifications like that').

11. RESTART AND TWO AT ONCE. Every mark lives on the billing source's row, written with the version check: the rest, the refusal, the waits, asking {stopKey, requestId} (only the writer that set it files the card), grant {to, stopKey, by, at}, switchNotified {stopKey, sessionIds}; the preset in notify_prefs; the card in the request store. Two stops landing together (a task run and a review, a run and a chat call) file one card, write one grant and send one notification. The wake, before every tick and before it takes the waits, ends the grants and closes the cards whose stop is over, also when it ended while the app was closed. No money decision is held in memory.

12. MONEY AND SECURITY. No budget, wrap-up line, monthly cap or share is passed: the hooks are unchanged; a task continued on the key is held by the same run, task, session, project and month caps; the card's figure is capped by the session's work budget left; a grant or a switch never raises anything. Under wait, before a yes and after Wait, the tests assert zero requests to the other credential's stand-in for every purpose. A key never runs through Claude Code (the continued run uses the loop driver). Card, chat, page and file text never becomes an instruction: the card's words are built from facts; chat answers the card only through the card command with the person's yes (medium risk); the per-turn press is a UI action, not text. Anthropic's refusal text is never shown and stays redacted in logs; marks hold no credential value.

13. ADR 0100 point 15's 'session lead's default' becomes the owner's rule.
alternatives_rejected: Two radio groups (which first; what then): the person must combine them, and it allows 'API key first, ask before subscription', which protects no money; five presets whose labels show the order read in one look.
Six presets (the safety design): the sixth is the one above; more choices for no money decision.

One order for every call for a person who never chose (the clarity design): it moves chat, planning and reviews from the API key to Claude Code (no money per reply, but slower, earlier turns quoted in one user turn, and under wait chat cannot answer until the reset), against ADR 0100 point 2; the owner did not decide it: owner question, the split kept and named meanwhile.
Keeping 'chat, planning and reviews always use the next one' (ADR 0100 point 4): moves work onto money while the app says it waits (7b).
A separate rule per kind of stop or per kind of call: the owner said a refusal follows the framework 'as if it has run out'; more knobs, more combinations to get wrong.
A per-project policy: the credentials and the plan's limits are the person's, shared by every project; what works now would depend on the page you are on; owner question, one for all meanwhile.
One ask card per task, per session or per project: one stop stops many tasks; one card per stop covers every project, review and plan until the stop ends.
A blocking ask card for a chat question alone (the clarity design): a money yes for every project to answer one question; the per-turn press is the smallest consent and spends nothing until pressed.
A yes that lasts until changed ('always use my API key'): that is 'Subscription first, then API key'; a grant for this stop keeps 'ask' meaning ask at the next stop.
A yes held in memory: Quit stops the service every day (ADR 0094); a forgotten yes would ask again or move without one.
Keeping the session alive while it asks: one active session per agent would block every other project's work for hours; it ends with a wait entry and the answer continues it as the person's start.

Keeping the share pause as a budget card: two behaviours for one stop (the card says it waits while the next pick moves to the key), and a raised allowance never ends it; the hooks still stop the run at the share, only what follows changes.

An API-key monthly limit field and a new caps level in the hooks (the safety design): no owner ask, a second money number beside the monthly cap, and a hooks change; Anthropic's own spend limit already rests the key; owner question.

Moving a task down to a credential that can do less at a stop (today's groups loop under use_other): the plan card said 'only it can'; the owner's rule of 2026-11-02 is another credential only when the first cannot do the task properly; it waits and says why.
Re-routing a running run back to the subscription when it resets: a run is never re-routed (ADR 0100 point 3) and the drivers differ; the next task uses it.
Trying a refused credential again after a while: repeated refused sign-ins can lock the person's account; only a different saved credential ends a refusal.
Treating the monthly cap of all spending as a stop that switches: subscription spend counts against it as its API-equivalent, so no switch can help; it stays ADR 0112's pause.
A notification for every switch, every task that moves, or every wait: once per stop and session, only for a move onto money the person did not just agree to; none for waiting (the owner).
An app-wide bar 'Claude is at its limit': a reminder-like element the owner does not want; the status lines, the run indicator, the Start dialog and Settings say it where the person acts.

Rewriting billing_order and mid_session_limit into the new key at upgrade: an older build after a downgrade would read nothing; a read-time mapping changes nothing, survives restarts by construction and keeps old Undo rows meaningful.

Offering the Start dialog's one-off 'Use API key' only under 'ask' (the clarity design): wait means the app does nothing by itself, not that the person cannot choose at Start; built under both, owner question.

decisions: CE-1 One policy: human.notify_prefs.credential_policy, one of subscription_then_wait, subscription_then_ask, subscription_then_key, key_then_subscription, key_only (packages/billing/src/policy.ts: CREDENTIAL_POLICIES; ruleOf(id) = {order, whenStopped: next | ask | wait, kinds}, key_only without the subscription; credentialPolicyOf(prefs) = the stored id, else derived at every read: billing_order with the subscription first + wait or unset -> subscription_then_wait, + use_other -> subscription_then_key, api_key or plan_credits first + wait -> key_only, + use_other -> key_then_subscription, no billing_order -> {chosen: false, the split order (tasks the routing policy's, every other call CALL_FALLBACK_ORDER), whenStopped wait, or next under use_other}; stopKeyOf(source, status); moneyRank). Why: the owner's 'a framework for what to use when, and then the system just does it'; read at every pick, so a change applies to the next call; deriving at read changes nothing a person chose and keeps ADR 0100 point 2 for a person who never chose (owner question).

CE-2 The router holds every stop: RouteContext.whenStopped replaces waitOnRest (waitOnRest still read as 'wait' for one release); the held list covers resting (reason limit), refused, plan_share (share, until the next month's start UTC) and monthly_limit (key_month), each with until and stopKey; under ask and wait a held first choice throws unavailable with details.waitFor {sourceId, kind, reason, until, stopKey, ask}; a grant {to, stopKey} on the held source whose stopKey is the current one lets the granted kind serve; next moves as today; RouteContext.heldNow (sources the caller saw stop on this call) are held like resting ones. Why: one place decides, so every caller agrees (7a, 7b, 7c).

CE-3 RouterTaskBilling.pick reads the policy at every pick for every purpose (session, critic, interactive, which D7's task check uses, chat, batch); the sources in req.exclude go to the router as heldNow, not as withheld, under ask and wait; at a stop it never moves to a lower chooser group: the task waits with reason needs. Why: one rule for every call; the exclude list today hides the very stop the hold must see; the plan card's 'only it can' stays true (ADR 0100 point 13).

CE-4 RoutedProvider follows the rule: after rest or refuse it picks again under the rule; under ask and wait the call ends with the wait (code unavailable, details.wait), which each caller handles as today: the critic's review waits in review without a counted try (review-refusal.ts), the plan waits (the intake's waitNow), chat holds (CE-9), a job skips (CE-10); under next one move as today, recorded with its cost (CE-11). holdNow(model) beside waitNow says whether a call would be held and whether a one-off switch could serve (for chat and d1109-chat-depth's thorough pass). Why: D5-1 is the main money leak today.

CE-5 A task its credential stopped keeps its work; under next, or after a grant, it goes back to the head of the session's queue and continues on the next credential in the same session; the brief's previous-run section for a usage_limit, credential_refused or share-stopped run is a sibling of whereTheLastRunStopped with exact text ('stopped when its Claude credential reached its limit' / 'was refused' / 'reached the share of the subscription Forerunner may use'), never 'It failed'; under ask and wait it waits, the session goes on with what can run and ends to wait (d1109-starts-engine's continuation goes on at the stop's end). Why: 7a ('the task to be completed by the API') without spending twice.

CE-6 Forerunner's share reached mid-run (the hooks' plan level, unchanged) returns as a credential stop with reason share and its handoff kept on the run (read by CE-5's brief): no budget card, the session does not end for it, the rule decides; the stop ends at the month's start or when the person raises the allowance (the share falls under the cap; the stop key changes). Budget cards at source 'plan' filed before the upgrade keep their wake (wakeBudgetWaits). Why: one behaviour per stop; a raised allowance must end the wait (U-052); no limit passed.

CE-7 Ask first: one card per stop (key credential:ask), filed only by the writer that set limits.asking {stopKey, requestId} with the version check, only when work needs it (a task run, a review, planning, the task check; not chat alone, not a job), the other credential can serve now and the caps have room for the waiting work's next call; its words from credential-words.ts, computed when shown. 'Use API key' re-reads the stop, writes limits.grant {to, stopKey, by: 'card', at} (version-checked; audit billing.grant), then: the waiting tasks of a session that still runs go back into it as its own tasks (d1109-starts-engine's admit handle; the runner's notAgain cleared for them), a session that ended to wait goes on now as the person's start (its continuation with by 'person'), a waiting plan is drafted, work outside a person's session stays ready for the next Start. 'Wait' closes the card and moves nothing; the asking mark keeps the stop, so no second card comes; recordWait(source, stopKey) records the same answer without a card, for the Start dialog's 'Start at 15:40' under ask (d1109-cred-screens), so no card follows the person's own choice. A second or late answer changes nothing and returns the card's Done line; an answer after the stop ended grants nothing. The wake, before takeReady, ends grants whose stop is over and withdraws open cards whose stop ended, whose other credential cannot serve any more, or whose preset changed. Why: 'after asking human' as one card; answered once; restart-safe; no start the person did not ask for (D6).

CE-8 A refusal follows the rule and always informs: one card per refusal, filed only by the writer that set the mark (concurrent refusals file one); refusalWhyOf(error) stores a category (expired sign-in, invalid or deleted key, not allowed for this model or workspace, other), never the provider's text; the card's body says what the work does under the rule (wait, next, or ask with Use API key / Wait, staying open as the fix-it card after an answer); a refused credential gets no second request from any path (a switch, a grant, a continuation, a late answer, chat, a job, the probe) until a different one is saved. Why: 7c; no retry that could lock the person's account.

CE-9 Chat asks holdNow before its model path; held: no model call and no ledger row, the hold reply written by code, with a per-turn 'Use API key' when the other credential serves now and the caps have room (the reply view's oneOff {label, explain}; the press runs that one question again with allowSwitch on that request only: no grant, no card; the route's flag for the press is d1109-cred-screens'); a standing grant or next: chat answers on the other credential and the reply's note says so once per stop per conversation; 'I could not answer (' never appears for a credential wait. Why: chat spends too (7b); the smallest consent; the person is in the chat.

CE-10 Background jobs (batch: the model watch and its evals, the monthly calibration) never ask and never switch under ask or wait: a held call spends nothing, files no card, logs one line, and the job is not marked done for its period, so the first tick after the stop runs it. Why: no card and no money for work nobody started.

CE-11 Switch data: the run row's artifacts carry switchedFrom {kind, stop}; the session log gets billing.switch {taskId, from, to, stop, until} once per stop and billing.back once when the first choice serves again; SessionResult.switched [{taskId, from, to, usdMicro}] summed from the ledger; CostView.byCredential (each billing source's spend in the view's window); RoutedProvider's fallback sentence in the person's time zone; the log lines from credential-words.ts. Why: every screen (d1109-cred-screens) reads data, not re-parsed sentences; 7a 'transparent'.

CE-12 One notification (credentialSwitched, normal urgency) per stop and session, only for a move onto money the policy made by itself inside a running session: not for a grant the person gave, not for a session whose Start dialog said it would run on the key, not for a move onto the subscription; deduplicated by limits.switchNotified {stopKey, sessionIds} (version-checked, restart-safe); none for a wait. Why: 7a and 7c ('notification or information'); the owner wants no notifications about waiting work.

CE-13 settings.set credential_policy: medium risk; narrows by moneyRank (subscription_then_wait 0, subscription_then_ask 1, subscription_then_key 2, key_then_subscription 3, key_only 3; not chosen counts 1 under wait, 2 under next), so a narrowing acts at once and a widening asks the person's yes; an agent actor is refused; an Undo is judged the same way; the settings_set tool definition lists credential_policy with its five values and neither legacy key; settings.set billing_order or mid_session_limit once credential_policy is stored, and an Undo of their old rows, answer 'This was replaced by "Which Claude does the work"; change it there.'. Why: money settings never widen by text; a tool definition is model-facing code.
root_causes: packages/billing/src/router.ts: the 'wait' rule (waitOnRest) was built for task runs and two kinds of stop (a rest, a refusal); the share and the key's monthly cap stayed plain skips, so they move work onto the next credential under any setting.

packages/runtime/src/wiring/billing-pick.ts: the sources a caller saw stop on this call are withheld before the router (exclude), and the groups loop moves to a lower chooser group on any 'no source' that is not a hold.

packages/runtime/src/provider/routed.ts: the non-task calls have their own one-time move to the next source, outside the person's setting, and their own fallback order (CALL_FALLBACK_ORDER) for a person who chose none.

packages/runtime/src/session/billing.ts and packages/commands/src/commands/settings.ts: an order and a mid-session rule as two settings with different reach per purpose; no value for asking and no state for an answer (asked, granted).
packages/runtime/src/session/executor.ts and budget-pause.ts: the subscription's share is enforced as a money budget level and handled as a budget pause, not as the subscription running out.
packages/runtime/src/session/task-context.ts: a credential-stopped run is read as a failed attempt although its work is kept.
packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts, routed.ts and notifications/producers.ts: a switch is a log sentence only; no fact on the run, the session or the result, no producer.
packages/runtime/src/session/credential-wait.ts and billing-pick.ts refuse(): filing a card is not tied to the version-checked mark that decided it, and the card stores no reason.

adr: Next free number (after the run C ADRs that take 0114 onward; the session lead numbers in merge order) — Which Claude does the work: one credential policy. The person picks one of five presets whose labels show the order: 'Subscription first, then wait', 'Subscription first, ask before API key', 'Subscription first, then API key', 'API key first, then subscription', 'API key only'. It is stored as human.notify_prefs.credential_policy and read at every pick by every model call: task runs, the critic's reviews, the plan from a brief, the task check, chat and the background jobs. Until a preset is stored the policy is read from billing_order and mid_session_limit and nothing is rewritten; a person who never set an order keeps ADR 0100 point 2's split (tasks on the subscription first, every other call on the API key first) with the rule from mid_session_limit, named in Settings (owner question). A stop is a usage limit, Forerunner's share of the subscription, a key's own monthly cap or a refusal; the budgets and the monthly cap of all spending are not stops and no switch passes them. 'wait': nothing calls another credential, for any purpose. 'ask': nothing moves until the person says yes on one Inbox card per stop, which states the cost in CHF and when the stop ends; the yes is a grant for that stop only, kept on the source row until the stop ends, and it is the person's start of the session that waited (D6). 'next': the work goes on at once, the stopped task too, continuing from its kept work; never onto a credential that cannot do what the plan card said only the first can. A refusal follows the same rule, files one card with what was refused, why in plain words and how to fix it, and the refused credential is never called again until a different one is saved. Every switch is recorded on the run, the session and the ledger and shown with its CHF; one notification per stop and session for a move onto money the person did not just agree to; none for waiting. Forerunner's share reached mid-run is a credential stop, not a budget pause; a raised allowance ends it. Closes wave7g6-triage owner_questions[1..3]. Amends ADR 0100 (points 2, 4, 10, 11, 13 and 15 and their amendments: the never-chosen split kept, the non-task one-time move replaced by the rule, 'Wait' extended to every call and every stop, the chooser's lower group no longer used at a stop, point 15 the owner's rule), 0044 (the share is a stop under the policy), 0098 (chat follows the preset onto Claude Code when the person puts the subscription first) and 0112 (point 6: the share no longer pauses as a budget).
